```{r}
#| label: fig-data-exploration-all
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "1-Week Time Course of All System Variables"

# Load core packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)
library(janitor)

# 1. Read and clean the data
hvac_data <- read_csv(here("data", "Turin", "HVAC_NE_EC_19-21.csv")) %>%
  clean_names()

# 2. Clean the timestamp and extract a subset
hvac_clean <- hvac_data %>%
  mutate(
    timestamp = ymd_hms(timestamp) 
  )

# Extract the first week of November
hvac_week <- hvac_clean %>%
  filter(
    timestamp >= ymd("2019-11-01", tz = "UTC"), 
    timestamp < ymd("2019-11-08", tz = "UTC")
  )

# 3. Plot all 10 variables
hvac_plot_all <- hvac_week %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -timestamp, 
    names_to = "Variable", 
    values_to = "Value"
  )

ggplot(hvac_plot_all, aes(x = timestamp, y = Value, color = Variable)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Comprehensive 1-Week HVAC Telemetry",
    subtitle = "Turin Dataset: Nov 1 - Nov 7, 2019",
    x = "Time", 
    y = "Measurement"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

- `power`: The power required by the fans [kW]. This is the instantaneous electrical demand. It shows a "block" pattern, representing the fan motors turning on, running at a steady state, and shutting off.
- `energy`: The energy required by the fans [kWh]. Power is the instantaneous rate, energy is the accumulated electricity consumed. The jagged, sawtooth pattern on top of the blocks is characteristic of accumulation over a 15-minute intervals.
- `rh_outdoor` (Outdoor Relative Humidity): The relative humidity of the outside air [%]. It dips during the warmest part of the day and peaks at night when the air cools.
- `rh_return` (Return Relative Humidity): The relative humidity of the return air [%]. Heating a volume of air lowers its relative humidity:  every time the system turns on to heat the space (`power`, `energy`), this indoor humidity drops.
- `rh_supply` (Supply Relative Humidity): The relative humidity of the supply air [%]. It tends to mirrors the return humidity but is physically altered by the heating coils.
- `sp_return (Setpoint Return)`: Tthe temperature setpoint of the return air [°C]. It represents the target temperature for the rooms.
- `t_outdoor (Outdoor Temperature)`: The ambient temperature outside [°C]. Natural diurnal (day/night) weather cycles.
- `t_return` (Return Temperature): The temperature of the air pulled back from the rooms into the HVAC unit [°C]: proxy for the actual room temperature.
- `t_saturation` (Saturation Temperature): The saturation temperature in the humidifier [°C]. Relates to the dew point the system maintains to prevent the air from becoming too dry when heated.
- `t_supply` (Supply Temperature): The temperature of the conditioned air being pushed into the rooms [°C]. To change the room temperature (t_return) to the target (sp_return), the system has to blast much warmer/colder air.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pairs-plot
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "Scatterplot matrix with correlation-mapped backgrounds (Sampled at n=5000)"

library(GGally)

# 1. Custom function to calculate correlation and map it to a background color
custom_scatter_bg <- function(data, mapping, ...) {
  x_data <- eval_data_col(data, mapping$x)
  y_data <- eval_data_col(data, mapping$y)
  
  corr <- cor(x_data, y_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  color_fun <- colorRamp(c("#f8766d", "white", "#00bfc4")) 
  scaled_corr <- (corr + 1) / 2 
  
  rgb_vec <- color_fun(scaled_corr)
  hex_color <- rgb(rgb_vec[1], rgb_vec[2], rgb_vec[3], maxColorValue = 255)
  
  ggplot(data, mapping) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = hex_color, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(...)
}

# 2. Generate the plot
p_pairs <- hvac_clean %>%
  select(-timestamp) %>% 
  sample_n(5000) %>% 
  ggpairs(
    lower = list(continuous = wrap(custom_scatter_bg, alpha = 0.1, size = 0.5)),
    upper = list(continuous = wrap(custom_scatter_bg, alpha = 0.1, size = 0.5)),
    title = "Pairwise Scatterplot Matrix (HVAC Telemetry)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA)
  )

p_pairs
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-network-graph

# install.packages(c("igraph", "ggraph")) # Run in console if needed
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Calculate the baseline correlation matrix (excluding timestamp)
cor_matrix <- cor(hvac_clean %>% select(-timestamp), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# 2. Threshold the matrix to create an unweighted adjacency matrix
#    Lowered to 0.8 to capture the primary temperature and humidity groupings
adj_matrix <- ifelse(abs(cor_matrix) > 0.8, 1, 0)

# 3. Remove self-loops (a variable is always perfectly correlated with itself)
diag(adj_matrix) <- 0

# 4. Convert the matrix into an undirected igraph object
g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj_matrix, mode = "undirected")

# 5. Plot the network graph
set.seed(42) # Ensures consistent spatial layout
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") + 
  geom_edge_link(color = "gray70", width = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_node_point(size = 14, color = "lightblue") +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), color = "black", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "HVAC Feature Dependency Network",
    subtitle = "Connected components defined by absolute correlation > 0.8"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-components-threshold
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Network fragmentation across correlation thresholds"

library(igraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# 1. Calculate the baseline correlation matrix (excluding timestamp)
cor_matrix <- cor(hvac_clean %>% select(-timestamp), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# 2. Define a sequence of thresholds from 0 to 0.99
thresholds <- seq(0, 0.99, by = 0.01)

# 3. Function to calculate number of components for a given threshold
count_components <- function(th) {
  # Create adjacency matrix for the current threshold
  adj_matrix <- ifelse(abs(cor_matrix) > th, 1, 0)
  diag(adj_matrix) <- 0
  
  # Build graph and count components
  g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj_matrix, mode = "undirected")
  components(g)$no
}

# 4. Map the function across all thresholds
component_counts <- map_dbl(thresholds, count_components)

# 5. Create a dataframe for plotting
df_thresh <- data.frame(
  Threshold = thresholds,
  Components = component_counts
)

# 6. Plot the relationship as a step-like function
ggplot(df_thresh, aes(x = Threshold, y = Components)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "navy", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 10, by = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Network Fragmentation Profile",
    subtitle = "Tracking how the feature graph breaks into isolated components",
    x = "Absolute Correlation Threshold (|r|)",
    y = "Number of Connected Components"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-spectral-analysis
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "Power Spectral Density (Frequency Domain)"

library(purrr)

# 1. Custom function to calculate the periodogram
get_periodogram <- function(series_name, data) {
  
  # Extract and mean-center the signal to remove the DC offset (0 frequency)
  x <- na.omit(data[[series_name]])
  x <- x - mean(x)
  
  n <- length(x)
  
  # Compute Fast Fourier Transform
  p <- Mod(fft(x))^2 / n
  
  # We only need the first half of the spectrum (Nyquist limit)
  half_n <- floor(n / 2)
  p <- p[2:(half_n + 1)] 
  
  # Frequencies: convert from cycles-per-observation to Cycles per Day (cpd)
  # 15 min intervals = 96 observations per day
  freq <- (1:half_n) / n * 96 
  
  tibble(
    Variable = series_name,
    Frequency_cpd = freq,
    Power = p
  )
}

# 2. Select key distinct variables representing weather, load, and effort
vars_to_analyze <- c("energy", "power", "rh_outdoor", "rh_return", "rh_supply",
                     "sp_return", "t_outdoor", "t_return", "t_saturation", "t_supply")
spectra_data <- map_dfr(vars_to_analyze, ~get_periodogram(.x, hvac_clean))

# 3. Plot the periodograms
ggplot(spectra_data, aes(x = Frequency_cpd, y = Power, color = Variable)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  # Focus strictly on low-frequency macro cycles (0 to 4 cycles per day)
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 2)) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 0:4, 
    labels = c("0", "1/day (24h)", "2/day (12h)", "3/day (8h)", "4/day (6h)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Spectral Decomposition of HVAC Telemetry",
    subtitle = "Identifying dominant cyclical periods via Fast Fourier Transform",
    x = "Frequency",
    y = "Spectral Power"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
  )
```

`power`: drop

`time_stamp`

`is_weekend` (from time_stamp)

`energy` (Raw State)

`energy_lag_24h` (Schedule context)

`energy_deriv_15m` (State transition context)

`rh_outdoor` (Raw context)

`rh_outdoor_lag_24h` (Weather shifts)

`delta_rh` =  `rh_return` - `rh_supply` (The active moisture control work)

`delta_rh_deriv_15m` (Sudden state changes in moisture control)

`t_outdoor` (Raw weather)

`t_outdoor_lag_24h` (Weather shift)

`t_saturation` (Raw state)

`t_saturation_deriv_15m` (Sudden humidifier faults)

`delta_t` = `t_return` - `t_supply` (The active heating work): 

`delta_t_deriv_15m` (Sudden loss or surge of heating power)

`temp_error` (How far off target the building is) $t\_return - sp\_return$

`sp_return`

```{r}
#| label: feature-engineering-pipeline
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(slider) 

hvac_features <- hvac_clean %>%
  # 0. Catch any stray NAs in the timestamp column before sequencing
  filter(!is.na(timestamp)) %>%
  # 1. Ensure the data is perfectly continuous in 15-minute increments
  complete(
    timestamp = seq(
      min(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE), 
      max(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE), 
      by = "15 mins"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(timestamp) %>%
  mutate(
    # 2. Context & Control
    is_weekend = if_else(wday(timestamp, week_start = 1) %in% c(6, 7), 1, 0),
    temp_error = t_return - sp_return,
    
    # 3. Common-Mode Rejection (Physics)
    delta_t = t_return - t_supply,
    delta_rh = rh_return - rh_supply
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # 4. Cyclical Lags
    t_outdoor_lag_24h = t_outdoor - lag(t_outdoor, n = 96),
    rh_outdoor_lag_24h = rh_outdoor - lag(rh_outdoor, n = 96),
    energy_lag_24h = energy - lag(energy, n = 96),
    
    # 5. Instantaneous Derivatives
    energy_deriv_15m = energy - lag(energy, n = 1),
    delta_t_deriv_15m = delta_t - lag(delta_t, n = 1),
    delta_rh_deriv_15m = delta_rh - lag(delta_rh, n = 1),
    t_return_deriv_15m = t_return - lag(t_return, n = 1),
    t_saturation_deriv_15m = t_saturation - lag(t_saturation, n = 1),
    
    # 6. Volatility 
    t_supply_roll_sd_1h = slider::slide_dbl(t_supply, sd, .before = 3, .complete = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # 7. Purge all artifacts (including the summer gap NAs)
  drop_na()

glimpse(hvac_features)
```


```{r}
#| label: fit-isolation-forest
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Isolation Forest Anomaly Scores over Time"

library(isotree)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Isolate the feature matrix (dropping the timestamp)
train_data <- hvac_features %>%
  select(-timestamp)

# 2. Fit the Isolation Forest
# ntrees = 500 ensures variance stabilization
# sample_size = 256 prevents anomaly masking
set.seed(42) 
iso_model <- isolation.forest(
  train_data,
  ntrees = 500,
  sample_size = 256,
  missing_action = "fail" # Our drop_na() ensures a clean matrix
)

# 3. Score the dataset
# predict() drops the data down the fitted forest and returns the bounded score [0, 1]
hvac_scored <- hvac_features %>%
  mutate(anomaly_score = predict(iso_model, train_data))

# 4. Visualize the temporal anomaly profile
ggplot(hvac_scored, aes(x = timestamp, y = anomaly_score)) +
  geom_line(color = "slategray", alpha = 0.8) +
  # Visual threshold for investigation (scores > 0.6 are generally considered anomalous)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "HVAC System Dynamic Anomaly Profile",
    subtitle = "Scores approaching 1.0 indicate severe structural breaks in mechanical behavior",
    x = "Time",
    y = "Anomaly Score (s)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-seed-stability
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Stability Check: Anomaly Scores across Random Seeds"

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Fit Model A 
iso_model_A <- isolation.forest(
  train_data,
  ntrees = 500,
  sample_size = 256,
  missing_action = "fail",
  seed = 42
)

# 2. Fit Model B 
iso_model_B <- isolation.forest(
  train_data,
  ntrees = 500,
  sample_size = 256,
  missing_action = "fail",
  seed = 123
)

# 3. Score and Combine
qc_data <- tibble(
  score_A = predict(iso_model_A, train_data),
  score_B = predict(iso_model_B, train_data)
)

# 4. Calculate Convergence Metric
stability_cor <- cor(qc_data$score_A, qc_data$score_B)

# 5. Visualize the Variance
ggplot(qc_data, aes(x = score_A, y = score_B)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5, color = "darkblue") +
  # Reference line for perfect agreement
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Isolation Forest Convergence Check",
    subtitle = sprintf("Pearson Correlation (Seed 42 vs Seed 123): %.4f", stability_cor),
    x = "Anomaly Score (Seed 42)",
    y = "Anomaly Score (Seed 123)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: calculate-p-values
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false

# 1. Fit the empirical distribution to the scores
score_ecdf <- ecdf(hvac_scored$anomaly_score)

# 2. Calculate percentiles and p-values
hvac_scored <- hvac_scored %>%
  mutate(
    percentile = score_ecdf(anomaly_score),
    # p-value: the probability of seeing a score this high or higher
    p_value = 1 - percentile 
  )

# 3. View the top anomalies with their new statistical context
top_anomalies_stat <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6) %>%
  arrange(desc(anomaly_score)) %>%
  select(
    timestamp, anomaly_score, p_value,
    is_weekend, sp_return, temp_error, delta_t
  )

# Display the top 5
head(top_anomalies_stat, 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: beta-mle-fit
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Empirical Density vs MLE Beta Distribution"

library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Calculate Method of Moments (MoM) to use as starting values for MLE
scores <- hvac_scored$anomaly_score
mu <- mean(scores)
var_x <- var(scores)

alpha_mom <- mu * ((mu * (1 - mu) / var_x) - 1)
beta_mom <- (1 - mu) * ((mu * (1 - mu) / var_x) - 1)

# 2. Fit the Beta distribution using Maximum Likelihood Estimation
beta_mle <- fitdistr(
  scores, 
  densfun = "beta", 
  start = list(shape1 = alpha_mom, shape2 = beta_mom)
)

alpha_est <- beta_mle$estimate["shape1"]
beta_est <- beta_mle$estimate["shape2"]

cat(sprintf("MLE Estimates:\nAlpha: %.4f\nBeta: %.4f\n\n", alpha_est, beta_est))

# 3. Superimpose the theoretical Beta curve on the empirical data
ggplot(hvac_scored, aes(x = anomaly_score)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 100, fill = "slategray", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Empirical Density (Dark Blue)
  geom_density(color = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
  # Theoretical Beta Density (Bright Red Dashed)
  stat_function(
    fun = dbeta, 
    args = list(shape1 = alpha_est, shape2 = beta_est), 
    color = "red", 
    linetype = "dashed", 
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Model Fit: Empirical Density vs MLE Beta Distribution",
    subtitle = "Red Dashed = Theoretical Beta Fit | Dark Blue = Empirical Data",
    x = "Anomaly Score (s)",
    y = "Density"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fault-signature-clustering
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false

# 1. Isolate the severe structural breaks
severe_anomalies <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6)

# 2. Select ONLY the physical/engineered features for clustering
# Explicitly using dplyr::select to prevent MASS collision
cluster_data <- severe_anomalies %>%
  dplyr::select(
    temp_error, delta_t, delta_rh,
    energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m,
    t_supply_roll_sd_1h
  )

# 3. Scale the data (Critical: Energy in kWh must not dominate Temp in Celsius)
cluster_scaled <- scale(cluster_data)

# 4. Compute Euclidean distance and build the hierarchical tree
dist_matrix <- dist(cluster_scaled, method = "euclidean")
hc_model <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "ward.D2")

# 5. Cut the tree into 3 distinct fault signatures
severe_anomalies <- severe_anomalies %>%
  mutate(fault_signature = as.factor(cutree(hc_model, k = 3)))

# 6. Summarize the mechanical profile of each fault signature
fault_profiles <- severe_anomalies %>%
  group_by(fault_signature) %>%
  summarize(
    event_count = n(),
    avg_temp_error = mean(temp_error, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_delta_t = mean(delta_t, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_energy_surge = mean(energy_deriv_15m, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_volatility = mean(t_supply_roll_sd_1h, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Display the diagnostic profiles
print(fault_profiles)
```

```{r}
# 1. Run Divisive Analysis (Top-Down)
diana_model <- diana(cluster_scaled, metric = "euclidean")

# 2. Cut the divisive tree into 3 distinct fault signatures
severe_anomalies <- severe_anomalies %>%
  mutate(fault_signature_diana = as.factor(cutree(as.hclust(diana_model), k = 3)))

# 3. Summarize the mechanical profile of the new DIANA signatures
fault_profiles_diana <- severe_anomalies %>%
  group_by(fault_signature_diana) %>%
  summarize(
    event_count = n(),
    avg_temp_error = mean(temp_error, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_delta_t = mean(delta_t, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_energy_surge = mean(energy_deriv_15m, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_volatility = mean(t_supply_roll_sd_1h, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Compare this output to the Ward's method table
print(fault_profiles_diana)
```

```{r}
#| label: explore-k-clusters
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true

library(purrr)

# Define a function to cut the DIANA tree and summarize the physics for any given k
get_profiles_for_k <- function(k_val) {
  severe_anomalies %>%
    mutate(cluster = as.factor(cutree(as.hclust(diana_model), k = k_val))) %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarize(
      k = k_val,
      n_events = n(),
      temp_err = round(mean(temp_error, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      delta_t = round(mean(delta_t, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      energy_surge = round(mean(energy_deriv_15m, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      volatility = round(mean(t_supply_roll_sd_1h, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Map over k = 2 through 5 and bind the results into one table
k_exploration <- map_dfr(2:5, get_profiles_for_k)

# Print the entire evolution table
print(k_exploration, n = 20)
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-expanded-clustering
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true

library(purrr)
library(cluster)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Expand the anomaly pool (lowering threshold from 0.60 to 0.55)
expanded_anomalies <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.55)

cat(sprintf("Expanded anomaly count: %d events\n\n", nrow(expanded_anomalies)))

# 2. Extract and scale the physics features
cluster_data_exp <- expanded_anomalies %>%
  dplyr::select(
    temp_error, delta_t, delta_rh,
    energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m,
    t_supply_roll_sd_1h
  )

cluster_scaled_exp <- scale(cluster_data_exp)

# 3. Run Divisive Analysis on the larger dataset
diana_exp <- diana(cluster_scaled_exp, metric = "euclidean")

# 4. Function to cut the tree and summarize
get_expanded_profiles <- function(k_val) {
  expanded_anomalies %>%
    mutate(cluster = as.factor(cutree(as.hclust(diana_exp), k = k_val))) %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarize(
      k = k_val,
      n_events = n(),
      temp_err = round(mean(temp_error, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      delta_t = round(mean(delta_t, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      energy_surge = round(mean(energy_deriv_15m, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      volatility = round(mean(t_supply_roll_sd_1h, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# 5. Map over k = 3 and 4 to check for structural changes
qc_exploration <- map_dfr(3:4, get_expanded_profiles)

print(qc_exploration, n = 10)
```
